source.title: Convolutional Normalization: Improving Deep Convolutional Network Robustness and Training
source.authors: Sheng Liu; Xiao Li; Yuexiang Zhai; Chong You; Zhi-Hui Zhu; C. Fernandez-Granda; Qing Qu

record.file_problem: Whole paper text, including appendices, is present.
record.tranche_reason: Compares training convergence with and without BatchNorm in classification experiments, using accuracy curves rather than a direct measure of time to training error.
record.gate_note: The paper reports ConvNorm and ConvNorm+BN results alongside BN and vanilla baselines. Its main textual convergence claim concerns ConvNorm; cited claims about other normalization methods are not this paper's results. Figure 4 and Figure 6 show accuracy curves, but the supplied text gives no exact curve values for BN versus vanilla.
record.test_reason: Figures 4 and 6 include matched networks with and without BatchNorm and accuracy versus training progress, directly testing V6's accuracy-speed component. VGG16 on CIFAR-10 overlaps the original setting. The supplied text does not preserve readable curve values or explicitly state the BN-versus-vanilla speed result, so its direction cannot be determined.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors conclude that ConvNorm accelerates convergence and improves robustness and generalization, and that combining it with BatchNorm can improve test performance while retaining fast convergence. They leave theoretical justification of the training benefits for future work.
record.recipe_differences: Adds a convolution-specific weight normalization and compares it with BatchNorm and other methods; does not isolate the full claim recipe for BN speed or learning-rate tolerance.
record.method_sensitivity: Architecture and dataset differ across the plotted convergence comparisons; results are shown for VGG16 and ResNet18 on CIFAR-10 and ResNet18 on ImageNet.

fits_no_version.finding: Section 4.2 reports that ConvNorm reaches comparable CIFAR-10 generalization performance in 1,000 iterations versus 8,000 with BatchNorm.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: ConvNorm can accelerate gains in test accuracy relative to BatchNorm in the tested recipes.

fits_no_version.finding: Table 4 reports ImageNet training failure for vanilla ResNet18 and 69.76% validation accuracy with BatchNorm. Endpoint test accuracy and failure status do not establish the claimed speed advantage.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: BatchNorm enables successful ImageNet ResNet18 training under this recipe.

fits_no_version.finding: Tables 6 and 7 measure test accuracy under label noise and data scarcity; they do not measure training-label fitting or convergence speed.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Normalization choices affect generalization under label noise and limited training data.

record.problems: The BN-versus-vanilla convergence curves are figure-only in the supplied text, with no exact values or explicit textual comparison. The stated convergence advantage is primarily for ConvNorm. The paper does not report training classification error for these comparisons.
record.rows_left_out: No rows: convergence curves that could compare BN with vanilla provide no recoverable exact values in the supplied text, and the paper's stated comparison does not explicitly establish the BN-versus-no-BN speed effect.

untested.parts: Near-zero training error is not established by readable results. Figure 6 does plot clean-label training accuracy, contrary to the record's blanket statement that training classification error is not reported; noisy-label experiments report test accuracy. Model-size and early-stopping effects are not tested.
No two-layer ReLU teacher-student problem, spurious-minimum frequency, or student-width comparison.
No controlled depth or identity-shortcut comparison, deep plain tanh experiment, or Fixup experiment.
No initialization comparison or measurement of trainable depth under different initializations.
No learning-rate stability threshold, curvature trajectory, or recovery above that threshold.

Higher-learning-rate tolerance, sigmoid MNIST networks, Inception, and Fixup are not tested. The direction and magnitude of the plotted BN-versus-vanilla speed comparison cannot be recovered from the supplied text.

record.verdict_notes: No verdict follows from ConvNorm outperforming BatchNorm: V6 compares adding BatchNorm with omitting it. The unreadable convergence comparisons are already declared in rows_left_out, so they are not duplicated in missing. No supplied result justifies a directional V6 label.

versions.untested_parts: Training classification error, random or corrupted labels, model size, and early stopping are not evaluated as stated in this version.
No two-layer ReLU teacher-student experiment or width sweep.
No depth comparison of plain networks with and without identity shortcuts, or tests of Fixup or deep plain tanh networks.
No comparison of initialization schemes or depth limits by initialization.
No learning-rate stability threshold, curvature, sharpness, or divergence experiment.

The paper includes BatchNorm in convergence comparisons, but does not state a BN-versus-no-BN speed result in text or provide curve values in the supplied text. It does not test tolerance to higher learning rates or Fixup.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
